paragraphs: We are a leading international supplier of equipment and services to global freight transportation markets. Through our wholly-owned subsidiaries and consolidated and unconsolidated joint ventures, we design, build and market freight railcars in North America, Europe and Brazil. We are a leading provider of freight railcar wheel services, component parts, maintenance and sustainable conversion services in North America. We own a lease fleet of railcars that originate primarily from our manufacturing operations. We offer railcar management, regulatory compliance services and leasing services to railroads and other railcar owners in North America.

We operate an integrated business model that combines freight car manufacturing, wheel services, railcar maintenance, component parts, leasing and fleet management services. Our model is designed to provide customers with a comprehensive set of freight car product and service solutions by utilizing our substantial engineering, mechanical and technical capabilities, as well as our experienced commercial personnel. Our integrated model allows us to develop cross-selling opportunities and synergies among our reportable segments thereby enhancing our margins. We believe our integrated model is difficult to duplicate and provides greater value for our customers and investors.

We operate in two reportable segments: Manufacturing and Leasing & Fleet Management. Effective September 1, 2024, we combined our former Maintenance Services and Manufacturing segments into a single reportable segment, Manufacturing. The combined Manufacturing reportable segment reflects a comprehensive production operation that allows us to streamline production processes and resources to better serve our customers. Separately, we renamed our former Leasing & Management Services reportable segment to Leasing & Fleet Management. These changes reflect the realignment of our organizational structure and reporting regularly provided to our chief operating decision maker to assess performance and allocate resources. These changes had no impact on our consolidated results of operations or financial position. Prior period segment results have been recast to reflect our new reportable segments. Financial information about our reportable segments as well as geographic information is located in Note 17 - Segment Information to the Consolidated Financial Statements.

References in this Annual Report on Form 10-K to the "Company," "Greenbrier," "we," "us" and "our" refer to The Greenbrier Companies, Inc. and, where appropriate, its subsidiaries. All references to years refer to the fiscal years ended August 31st unless otherwise noted.

The Greenbrier Companies, Inc., is incorporated in Oregon. Our principal executive offices are located at One Centerpointe Drive, Suite 200, Lake Oswego, Oregon 97035. Our telephone number is (503) 684-7000 and our Internet website is located at http://www.gbrx.com. Information contained on our website is not part of or incorporated into this Form 10-K or any other filings with the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC).

North American Manufacturing - We manufacture most freight railcar types currently in use in the North American market (other than coal cars) and we continue to expand our product features and functionality. We have demonstrated an ability to capture high market shares in many of the car types we produce. The primary products we produce for the North American market are:

Freight Railcars - We produce a variety of covered hopper cars for food grade products, grain, fertilizer, cement, minerals and plastic pellets as well as gondolas and open top hoppers for steel, metals, scrap and aggregates. We also produce a wide range of boxcars, which are used in the transport of paper products, perishables and general merchandise. Our flat car products include center partition cars for the forest products industry and heavy-duty flat cars.

Tank Cars - We produce a variety of tank cars, including general purpose, pressurized, coiled, lined, insulated and stainless steel. These are designed for the transportation of hazardous and non-hazardous commodities such as
petroleum products, ethanol, liquefied petroleum gas, petrochemicals, caustic soda, chlorine, fertilizers, vegetable oils, bio-diesel and various other products.

Intermodal Railcars - We manufacture a comprehensive portfolio of intermodal railcars. Our most popular intermodal product is our double-stack railcars called Maxi-Stack® I and Maxi-Stack® IV. The double-stack railcar is designed to transport containers stacked two-high on a single platform and provides significant operating and capital savings over other types of intermodal railcars.

Automotive - We manufacture a full line of railcar equipment specifically designed for the transportation of light vehicles. Our automotive offerings include the Auto-Max® II, Multi-MaxTM and Multi-Max PlusTM products, which are designed to carry automobiles, CUVs, SUVs, trucks and high sided vans efficiently.

Sustainable ConversionsTM - We are a leading provider of sustainable conversions, which repurposes existing railcars into equipment for other service. Our sustainable conversions are an efficient and cost-savings option for railcar owners looking to diversify and optimize their fleets. We rebody or stretch covered hoppers into larger cubic service, re-rack or perform deck conversion on auto racks, and perform tank car retrofits to help customers manage pending regulations.

Wheel Services - We operate a wheel services network in North America. Our wheel shops provide complete wheel services including reconditioning of wheels and axles in addition to new axle machining, finishing and downsizing.

Railcar Maintenance - We operate a railcar maintenance network in North America including shops certified by the Association of American Railroads (AAR). Our shops perform routine railcar maintenance for third parties and for our leased and managed railcar fleets.

headings: Risks Related to Our Business
An economic downturn and economic uncertainty may adversely affect demand for our products and services.

Changes in global trade policies, including imposed and threatened tariffs by the U.S. and reciprocal tariffs by its trading partners, remain uncertain and could impact our financial condition or results of operations.
Increases in the price of materials and components used in the production of our products could negatively impact our profit margin on the sale of our products.
Shortages of skilled labor, increased labor costs, or failure to maintain good relations with our workforce could adversely affect our operations.
Disruptions in the supply of materials and components used in the production of our products could negatively impact our business and results of operations.

Our business and financial results of operations could be materially and adversely impacted if we fail to adequately manage and respond to events that cause an interruption or interference in our business operations.
We face risks related to cybersecurity threats and incidents that increase our costs and could disrupt our business and operations, damage our reputation, and result in material liabilities.
Our backlog is not necessarily indicative of the level of our future revenues.
We operate in highly competitive industries. We may not be able to sustain our market leadership positions, which may impact our financial results.
The timing of our asset sales and related revenue recognition could cause significant differences in our quarterly results and liquidity.
We may be unable to effectively implement capacity rationalization initiatives, cost reductions and/or restructuring efforts and our business might be adversely affected.
We derive a significant amount of our revenue from a limited number of customers, the loss of or reduction of business from one or more of which could have an adverse effect on our business.
Our business may be negatively impacted as a result of war in Ukraine, as well as civil unrest and armed conflict in other geographies.
Our debt could have negative consequences to our business or results of operations.
A failure to design or manufacture products or technologies or to achieve timely certification or market acceptance of new products or technologies could have an adverse effect on our profitability.
Our product and service warranties could expose us to significant claims.
Insurance coverage could be costly, unavailable or inadequate.
Our financial performance and market value could cause write-downs of goodwill or intangibles or other long-lived assets in future periods.
Our business will suffer if we are unsuccessful in making, integrating, and maintaining acquisitions, joint ventures and other strategic investments.
Risks Related to Market and Economic Factors
Cyclical economic downturns in our industry usually result in decreased demand for our products and services and reduced revenue.
Risks related to our operations outside of the U.S. could adversely affect our operating results.
The types of rail equipment we sell and the services we provide significantly impact our revenue and our margin and are dependent on broad economic trends over which we have little or no control.
Demand for our railcar equipment and services is dependent on the future of rail transportation and the manner in which railroads operate.
Fluctuations in foreign currency exchange rates could lead to increased costs and lower profitability.
Some of our competitors are owned or financially supported by foreign governments and may sell products below cost or otherwise compete unfairly.
Fires, natural disasters, pandemics, terrorism, or severe or unusual weather conditions could disrupt our business and result in loss of revenue or higher expenses or decreased demand.
Risks Related to Legal, Compliance and Regulatory Matters
Train derailments or other accidents could subject us to legal claims that adversely impact our business, financial condition and our results of operations.
Risks related to potential misconduct by employees may adversely impact us.
Changes in, or failure to comply with, applicable regulations may adversely impact our business, financial condition and results of operations.
We have potential exposure to environmental liabilities, which could increase our operating costs or have an adverse effect on our results of operations.

Business, regulatory, and legal developments regarding climate change may increase our operating costs, and may negatively affect the demand for our products or the ability of our critical suppliers to meet our needs.
paragraphs: The following risks could materially and adversely affect our business, financial condition, operating results, liquidity and cash flows, prospects, and stock price. These risks do not identify all risks that we face; other factors, events, or uncertainties currently unknown to us or that we currently do not consider to present significant risks to our business or that emerge in the future could affect us adversely.

Our customers are often able to delay replacing rail equipment during economic downturns. Factors affecting the level of customer spending for our products and services include general economic conditions, such as inflation, slower economic growth and the potential for a recession and other factors such as business confidence in future economic conditions, changing trade policies and the availability and cost of efficient capital, among other factors. Domestic and worldwide economic conditions remain uncertain. As global economic conditions continue to be volatile or economic uncertainty increases, trends in business spending may become increasingly unpredictable and subject to reductions and fluctuations. Unfavorable economic conditions may lead our customers to delay or reduce purchases of our products and services, result in lower sales volumes, lower prices, lower lease utilization rates, and decreased revenues and profits.

The current U.S. presidential administration has announced a wide range of tariffs on imports from many countries. In response to these tariffs, certain of the impacted countries have announced, and in some cases imposed, counter tariffs on goods that are imported from the U.S. The imposition of such tariffs have resulted in increased costs. We are continuing to monitor the rapidly evolving tariff and global trade policies and are working with our suppliers to mitigate potential impacts on our business. The extent and duration of the tariffs and the resulting impact on general economic conditions and on our business are uncertain and depend on various factors, such as recent legal challenges to the U.S.'s imposition of tariffs, negotiations between the U.S. and affected countries, the responses of other countries or regions, relief that may be granted, availability and cost of alternative sources of supply and demand for our products in affected markets. The uncertainty of the tariffs, including a potential increase in costs and decrease in demand for our products, could heighten the other risks factors and uncertainties discussed in this Item 1A, or in other reports we periodically file with the SEC, and impact our financial condition or results of operations. Furthermore, our competitors may be less exposed to tariff impacts or in a better position to mitigate the increased costs of tariffs.

A significant portion of our business depends on the adequate supply of steel, other raw materials, and energy, as well as numerous specialty parts and components, such as brakes, wheels, side frames, bolsters, and bearings for the railcar business, at cost-effective prices. The cost of steel and all other materials used in the production of our railcars represents more than half of our direct manufacturing costs per railcar. If we are not able to purchase materials and energy at competitive prices, our ability to produce and sell our products on a cost-effective basis could be adversely impacted which, in turn, could adversely affect our revenue and profitability.

We depend on skilled labor in all areas of our business. Some of our facilities are located in areas where demand for skilled labor often exceeds supply. A shortage of some types of skilled labor such as welders and machine operators would restrict our ability to maintain or increase production rates, lead to production inefficiencies and increase our labor costs. Due to the competitive nature of the labor markets in which we operate and the cyclical nature of the railcar industry, the resulting employment cycle increases our risk of not being able to recruit, train and retain the employees we require at efficient costs and on reasonable terms, particularly when competition for such skilled labor increases. If we lose our reputation as a leader in safety among our industry peers, we may become less competitive

in our efforts to attract such skilled labor. Further, we are party to collective bargaining agreements with labor unions at some of our operating sites. Disputes with labor unions, could result in, among other things, strikes, work stoppages or other slowdowns which could cause a significant disruption of our operations and increase our ongoing labor costs. We cannot be assured that our relations with our workforce will remain positive. If we are unable to recruit, train and retain adequate numbers of qualified employees and third-party labor providers on a timely basis or at a reasonable cost or on reasonable terms, our business and results of operations could be adversely affected.

paragraphs: 1. Manufacturing - We design, build and market freight railcars in North America and Europe. We are also a leading provider of freight railcar wheel services, component parts, maintenance and retrofitting services in North America.

2. Leasing & Fleet Management - We own a lease fleet of railcars that originate primarily from our manufacturing operations. We offer railcar management, regulatory compliance services and leasing services to railroads and other railcar owners in North America. We also place railcars on lease to customers and sell the railcars with leases attached to investors.
We operate an integrated business model which we believe is difficult to duplicate and provides greater value for our customers and investors.

We continue to operate in an environment characterized by ongoing macroeconomic uncertainty, including inflationary pressures, potential impacts from global trade tensions and tariffs and volatility in foreign exchange and interest rates. We believe that a sustained economic slowdown or continued supply chain disruption could significantly affect our operations and financial performance. Such developments could impact our business both directly and indirectly. Direct impacts may include higher costs for raw materials, labor and manufacturing inputs. Indirectly, a weaker macroeconomic environment could reduce demand for new railcar orders and leasing activity.

Despite these potential headwinds, we believe we are well-positioned to continue to execute on our multi-year strategy. In addition, we believe our integrated business model provides flexibility across economic cycles. We maintain a diversified customer base and disciplined approach to managing working capital and operating costs.
While we believe that macroeconomic uncertainty is affecting demand across the markets in which we operate, we delivered strong results in 2025, which included the following:
• Expanded our Margin as a percentage of Revenue from 15.8% in 2024 to 18.7% in 2025.
• Increased Net earnings attributable to Greenbrier by $44.0 million or 27.5% compared to the prior year.
• Generated $266 million of Net cash provided by operating activities.
• Increased our owned lease fleet by 1,500 railcars, representing a 9.7% increase since August 31, 2024.
• Renewed and extended our $600 million domestic revolving facility and $250 million term loan in May 2025, extending the maturity date of both instruments until 2030.

We believe our results highlight our continued focus on our strategic plan as we remain focused on increasing recurring revenue, expanding aggregate gross margin and raising return on invested capital. Recurring revenue is defined as Leasing & Fleet Management revenue excluding the impact of syndication transactions.

With a global footprint, supply chain and customer base, we are focused on navigating the impact of changing trade policies, such as tariffs, as well as general geopolitical and macroeconomic uncertainty.

paragraphs: 本公司為全球貨運運輸市場的國際領先設備與服務供應商。透過我們的 wholly-owned 子公司及合併與未合併之合資企業，我們在北美、歐洲與巴西設計、製造並行銷貨運鐵路車輛。本公司為北美地區貨運鐵路車輛輪子服務、零組件、維護及可持續轉換服務的領先供應商。本公司擁有來自我們製造作業的租賃車輛隊伍。我們為北美地區的鐵路公司及其他車輛所有者提供車輛管理、法規合規服務及租賃服務。
我們運作一個整合的商業模式，結合貨運車輛製造、輪子服務、車輛維護、零組件、租賃及車隊管理服務。我們的模式設計為透過我們深厚的工程、機械及技術能力，以及經驗豐富的商業人員，為客戶提供完整的貨運車輛產品與服務解決方案。我們的整合模式使我們能夠在應報告分部之間發展交叉銷售機會與協同效應，從而提高我們的毛利率。我們認為我們的整合模式難以複製，並為客戶與投資者提供更高的價值。

我們運作兩個應報告分部：製造與租賃及車隊管理。自 2024 年 9 月 1 日起，我們將原先的維護服務與製造分部合併為單一應報告分部，製造。合併後的製造應報告分部反映了一個全面的生產作業，使我們能夠優化生產流程與資源，以更好地服務客戶。另外，我們將原先的租賃及管理服務應報告分部更名為租賃及車隊管理。這些變更反映了我們組織結構與報告的重新調整，並定期提供給我們首席運營決策者以評估績效與分配資源。這些變更對我們的合併財務狀況或營運成果無影響。前一時期的分部結果已重新調整以反映我們的新應報告分部。有關應報告分部及地理資訊的財務資訊，請參閱第 17 註 - 分部資訊，於合併財務報表中。
本年度報告表 10-K 中提及的 "本公司"、"Greenbrier"、"我們"、"我們"及 "我們"均指 The Greenbrier Companies, Inc. 及，如適用，其子公司。所有提及年份均指財務年度結束於 8 月 31 日，除非另有說明。

The Greenbrier Companies, Inc. 為 Oregon 州公司。我們的總部位於 One Centerpointe Drive, Suite 200, Lake Oswego, Oregon 97035。我們的電話號碼為 (503) 684-7000，我們的網站為 http://www.gbrx.com。網站上的資訊並非本表 10-K 或任何其他向美國證券交易委員會 (SEC) 提交的文件的一部分或其組成部分。
北美製造 - 我們製造目前北美市場（除煤炭車外）使用的大多數貨運鐵路車輛類型，並持續擴展我們的產品功能與特性。我們已展現出在許多我們製造的車輛類型中取得高市場佔有率的能力。我們為北美市場製造的主要產品為：
貨運鐵路車輛 - 我們製造多種覆蓋式散裝車，用於食品級產品、穀物、肥料、水泥、礦物及塑膠粒，以及敞車與開頂散裝車，用於運輸鋼鐵、金屬、廢料及集料。我們也製造廣泛的箱型車，用於運輸紙製品、易腐品及一般商品。我們的平板車產品包括用於木材產業的中間隔板車及重型平板車。
槽車 - 我們製造多種槽車，包括一般用途、加壓、捲軸、內襯、絕緣及不銹鋼槽車。這些車輛設計用於運輸危險與非危險商品，例如
石油產品、乙醇、液化石油氣、石化產品、氫氧化鈉、氯氣、肥料、植物油、生物柴油及各種其他產品。
多式聯運貨車 - 我們製造一整套多式聯運貨車。我們最暢銷的多式聯運產品為雙層堆疊貨車，稱為 Maxi-Stack® I 與 Maxi-Stack® IV。雙層堆疊貨車設計用於運輸兩層堆疊的貨櫃，並在單一平台上運輸，相比其他類型的多式聯運貨車，可提供顯著的運營與資本節省。
汽車 - 我們製造一整套專為輕型車輛運輸設計的貨車設備。我們的汽車產品包括 Auto-Max® II、Multi-MaxTM 與 Multi-Max PlusTM，這些產品設計用於高效運輸汽車、跨界休旅車、SUV、貨車與高側貨車。
永續轉型TM - 我們是永續轉型的領導供應商，將現有貨車轉型為其他服務的設備。我們的永續轉型為貨車所有者提供高效且節省成本的選擇，使其能多元化並優化其車隊。我們會重新打造或延長覆蓋散裝貨車以提供更大的立方空間，重新架設或進行貨車平台轉換，並進行槽車翻新，以協助客戶應對即將來臨的規範。
輪胎服務 - 我們在北美運營一個輪胎服務網路。我們的輪胎工廠提供完整的輪胎服務，包括輪胎與軸承的重製，以及新軸承的加工、完工與縮小。
貨車維護 - 我們在北美運營一個貨車維護網路，包括經美國鐵路協會（AAR）認證的工廠。我們的工廠為第三方及我們租賃與管理的貨車車隊提供常規貨車維護服務。

paragraphs: 1. 製造業 - 我們設計、製造並行銷 freight railcars 在北美與歐洲。我們同時也是北美地區主要的 freight railcar 輪胎服務、零組件、維護與翻新服務供應商。
2. 租賃與車隊管理 - 我們擁有來自我們製造業務的租賃車隊。我們為北美地區的鐵路公司及其他車隊所有者提供車隊管理、法規合規服務及租賃服務。我們同時將 railcars 租賃給客戶，並以附有租賃條款的方式出售給投資者。
我們運作一個整合型商業模式，我們認為此模式難以複製，並為我們的客戶與投資者提供更高的價值。
我們持續在一個總體經濟不確定性持續存在的環境中運作，包括通貨膨脹壓力、全球貿易緊張關係與關稅的潛在影響，以及外匯與利率的波動。我們認為，持續的經濟減速或供應鏈中斷可能會顯著影響我們的運作與財務表現。這些發展可能會直接或間接影響我們的業務。直接影響可能包括原材料、勞動力與製造投入成本的提高。間接影響方面，較弱的總體經濟環境可能會減少新車訂單與租賃活動的需求。
儘管這些潛在的挑戰，我們認為我們處於一個良好的位置，可以持續執行我們的多年策略。此外，我們認為我們的整合型商業模式在經濟週期中提供了靈活性。我們維持多元化的客戶羣體，並採用嚴謹的作法來管理營運資金與營運成本。
雖然我們認為總體經濟不確定性正在影響我們所處市場的需求，但我們在 2025 年仍取得了強勁的表現，包括以下內容：
• 毛利率佔營業收入的百分比從 2024 年的 15.8% 提高至 2025 年的 18.7%。
• 比上一年度增加 44.0 百萬美元或 27.5% 的淨營業收入歸屬於 Greenbrier。
• 產生 266 百萬美元之營運活動提供之淨現金。
• 將自有租賃車隊增加 1,500 輛鐵路貨車，較 2024 年 8 月 31 日成長 9.7%。
• 2025 年 5 月續約並延長我們之 6 億美元國內循環信貸設施及 2.5 億美元定期貸款，將兩項工具之到期日延長至 2030 年。
我們認為我們的結果顯示我們持續著力於戰略計畫，我們仍專注於提升經常性收入、擴大總體毛利率及提高投入資本回報率。經常性收入定義為租賃及車隊管理收入，扣除 syndication 交易之影響。
憑藉全球據點、供應鏈及客戶羣，我們專注於應對變動貿易政策（如關稅）以及總體經濟與地緣政治不確定性之影響。

headings: 與我們業務相關的風險
經濟衰退與經濟不確定性可能不利於我們產品與服務的需求。
全球貿易政策的變動，包括美國所施加與威脅施加的關稅，以及其貿易夥伴所施加的報復性關稅，仍存在不確定性，可能會影響我們的財務狀況或營運結果。
用於我們產品生產的材料與零組件價格上漲，可能會不利於我們產品銷售的毛利率。
缺乏技術性勞工、勞動成本增加，或未能維持與我們員工的良好關係，可能會不利於我們的營運。
用於我們產品生產的材料與零組件供應中斷，可能會不利於我們的業務與營運結果。
若我們未能充分管理與回應導致我們業務營運中斷或幹擾的事件，可能會對我們的業務與財務營運結果造成重大且不利的影響。
我們面臨與網路安全威脅與事件相關的風險，這些風險會增加我們的成本，並可能幹擾我們的業務與營運，損害我們的聲譽，並導致重大賠償責任。
本公司未結餘並不一定反映未來營業收入之水準。
本公司所處產業為高度競爭性產業。本公司可能無法維持市場領導地位，此情形可能影響本公司之財務結果。
本公司資產出售之時點及相關收入認列，可能導致本公司每季之營運結果與流動性出現顯著差異。
本公司可能無法有效執行產能優化措施、成本削減及/或重整計畫，本公司業務可能因此受到不利影響。
本公司來自有限數量客戶之營業收入佔相當大比例，若其中一或多個客戶業務流失或減少，可能對本公司業務造成不利影響。
本公司業務可能因烏克蘭戰爭，以及其他地區之民變與武裝衝突而受到負面影響。
本公司之債務可能對本公司業務或營運結果產生負面影響。
若無法設計或製造產品或技術，或未能及時取得新產品或技術之認證或市場接受度，可能對本公司獲利能力造成不利影響。
本公司產品及服務的保固可能使我們面臨重大索賠。
保險覆蓋範圍可能成本高昂、無法取得或不足。
本公司財務表現與市場價值可能導致未來期間對商譽、無形資產或其他長期資產的減損提列。
若本公司未能成功進行產品整合與維護併購、合資企業及其他戰略投資，將對本公司業務造成影響。
與市場及經濟因素相關之風險
我們產業所面臨的週期性經濟衰退通常導致我們產品與服務之需求減少，以及營收下降。
與本公司於美國境外之營運相關之風險可能對本公司營運成果造成不利影響。
本公司所銷售之鐵路設備類型及所提供的服務，顯著影響本公司之營收與毛利率，且取決於廣泛之經濟趨勢，而本公司對此等趨勢幾乎毫無控制力。
本公司鐵路車輛設備及服務的需求取決於鐵路運輸的未來發展以及鐵路運營的方式。
外幣交換率的波動可能導致成本增加及利潤率下降。
部分競爭對手為外國政府所擁有或財務支持，可能以低於成本價格銷售產品或以其他方式不公平競爭。
火災、自然災害、疫情、恐怖主義或嚴重或異常天氣條件可能幹擾本公司業務，導致收入減少或費用增加或需求下降。
與法律、合規及監管事項相關的風險
火車脫軌或其他事故可能使本公司面臨法律聲請，不利於本公司業務、財務狀況及營運成果。
與員工潛在不當行為相關的風險可能對本公司造成不利影響。
適用規範的變更，或未能遵守適用規範，可能對本公司業務、財務狀況及營運成果造成不利影響。
本公司可能面臨環境責任相關風險，此等風險可能提高本公司營運成本，或對本公司營業成果產生不利影響。
有關氣候變遷的業務、法規及法律發展，可能提高本公司營運成本，並可能對本公司產品之需求，或關鍵供應商履行本公司需求之能力產生負面影響。
paragraphs: 下列風險可能對我們的業務、財務狀況、營運成果、流動性及現金流、前景及股票價格造成重大且不利的影響。這些風險並未涵蓋我們所面臨的所有風險；其他因素、事件或不確定性，目前我們尚未知悉，或目前認為對我們業務並無重大影響，未來亦可能出現，這些都可能對我們造成不利影響。

我們的客戶經常能在經濟衰退期間延後更換鐵路設備。影響我們產品與服務客戶支出水平的因素包括總體經濟狀況，例如通貨膨脹、經濟成長放緩及經濟衰退的潛在風險，以及其他因素，例如對未來經濟狀況的企業信心、貿易政策的變動以及高效資金的可取得性與成本，等等。國內與國際經濟狀況仍不確定。隨著全球經濟狀況持續波動或經濟不確定性增加，企業支出的趨勢可能變得更加難以預測，並可能出現減少與波動。不利的經濟狀況可能導致我們的客戶延後或減少購買我們的產品與服務，造成銷售量減少、價格下降、租賃使用率降低，以及收入與利潤減少。

目前美國總統政府已宣佈對來自許多國家的進口商品徵收廣泛的關稅。為回應這些關稅，一些受影響的國家已宣佈，並在某些情況下已實施對從美國進口商品的反制關稅。這些關稅的實施導致成本增加。我們持續監測快速變化的關稅與全球貿易政策，並與供應商合作以緩解對我們業務的潛在影響。關稅的範圍與持續時間，以及對總體經濟狀況與我們業務的影響，仍不確定，並取決於多種因素，例如近期對美國徵收關稅的法律挑戰、美國與受影響國家之間的談判、其他國家或地區的回應、可能提供的緩衝措施、替代供應來源的可取得性與成本，以及受影響市場中我們產品的需求。關稅的不確定性，包括成本可能增加與我們產品需求下降的潛在風險，可能加劇本項目1A或其他我們定期向證券交易委員會提交報告中所討論的其他風險因素與不確定性，並影響我們的財務狀況或營運成果。此外，我們的競爭對手可能對關稅影響的暴露較低，或處於較佳的減緩關稅成本增加的優勢地位。

我們業務的很大一部分依賴於鋼鐵、其他原材料與能源的充足供應，以及眾多專用零件與零組件，例如鐵路車輛業務中的剎車、輪子、側架、 bolster（加強件）與軸承，這些在成本效益的價格下取得。鋼鐵及其他用於我們鐵路車輛生產的材料成本，代表我們每輛鐵路車輛直接製造成本的超過一半。如果我們無法以具競爭力的價格購買材料與能源，我們以成本效益方式生產與銷售產品的能力可能受到不利影響，進而對我們的收入與利潤造成不利影響。

我們在業務各個領域都依賴具專業技能的勞工。我們一些設施位於需求經常高於供給的地區。某些類型具專業技能的勞工，例如焊工與機械操作員的短缺，將限制我們維持或提高生產速度的能力，導致生產效率低下，並增加我們的勞工成本。由於我們所處勞工市場的競爭性與鐵路車輛產業的週期性，導致就業週期增加我們無法以有效成本與合理條件招募、培訓與留住所需員工的風險，特別是在對具專業技能勞工的競爭增加時。如果我們失去在業界同儕中作為安全領導者的聲譽，我們可能變得較不具競爭力。
在吸引這些具專業技能勞工的 endeavour（努力）中。此外，我們在一些運營場地與勞工工會簽訂集體談判協議。與勞工工會的爭議，可能導致罷工、停工或其他減速措施，這些都可能對我們的運營造成重大幹擾，並增加我們的持續勞工成本。我們無法保證我們與員工的關係會持續正面。如果我們無法及時或以合理成本與條件招募、培訓與留住足夠的合格員工與第三方勞工供應商，我們的業務與營運成果可能受到不利影響。
